short: The general who won the war, then spent eight years trying to enforce its outcome.
full:
Grant came to the presidency in 1869 as the most successful Union commander, with no political experience and little appetite for the trade. He used federal power against the Ku Klux Klan, sending troops and prosecutors into South Carolina under the Enforcement Acts of 1870 and 1871 and effectively destroying the first Klan.

He backed the Fifteenth Amendment, ratified in 1870, and signed the Civil Rights Act of 1875. His administrations were also badly corrupt: the Credit Mobilier railway scheme, the Whiskey Ring, and the impeachment of his war secretary, though Grant himself took nothing. The Panic of 1873 crippled the economy for the rest of his tenure and drained northern willingness to police the South. The disputed election of 1876 was settled just after he left by a bargain that withdrew the remaining troops and ended Reconstruction.
